Golden and naive locations narrow `sql` to the map / string form respectively via `goldenStatements` / `naiveStatements`.

binds.description: Bind values for the `?` placeholders in this statement's `sql`. Follows the same scalar-or-dialect-keyed polymorphism as `sql`: a flat ordered array when the bind holes are shared across dialects (the authored default), OR a dialect-keyed map of arrays when the hole structure diverges (e.g. Postgres carries per-segment JSON keys while MariaDB carries one `'$.a.b'` path bind). When a map, its keys MUST equal this entry's `sql` map's keys (harness-asserted). Defaults to empty.

goldenStatements.description: An ordered list of golden statement entries — the shared `statementEntry`, with `sql` narrowed to the dialect-keyed map form (dialect texts side by side).

naiveStatements.description: An ordered list of naive statement entries — the shared `statementEntry`, with `sql` narrowed to the plain-string form (dialect-agnostic SQL run verbatim on every dialect).

bareWriteRow.description: The BARE neutral write row (①) at the one location an instruction may stand in its place — `when.write`, whose four forms a reader dispatches on the members the input itself carries (`target` the predicate-selected instruction, `rows` the keyed one, an array the multi-key conflict form, anything else this). That dispatch is only sound if the two discriminators are RESERVED from the row's own open vocabulary, so this is `$defs/writeRow` with `target` and `rows` forbidden. Without the reservation the row branch swallows both instruction forms — every instruction is also a row, since an instruction's members are all admissible `writeRowValue`s — so the instruction branches would add no validity and a legitimate row naming a `many` value object `rows` would be silently re-read as a keyed instruction by every dispatcher. The reservation is POSITIONAL, exactly like the `observedTxStart` / `observedValidStart` refusal one `$defs` below: it holds where the ambiguity is, so a row inside the multi-key ARRAY form — unambiguous by JSON type — keeps the full vocabulary. A model whose entity really does declare a member named `target` or `rows` therefore cannot author a bare `when.write` for it; the row is REFUSED here rather than reclassified, because a silent reclassification is what turns an authoring mistake into a case that grades the wrong rule.

writeRow.description: A flat attribute-named write row at a FLUSH / MATERIALIZATION location (an m-opt-lock conflict / retry write, a writeSequence step) — the neutral write input (①), same vocabulary as a fixture row, PLUS the reserved framework-owned `observedVersion` control key. It is the canonical durable instruction row (`write-instruction.schema.json#/$defs/writeRow`) with ONE difference: `observedVersion` is legitimate FLUSH-TIME context here (the version the unit of work observed, whether the write goes on to gate on it, advance from it, or merely be licensed by the read that recorded it), whereas the canonical durable instruction FORBIDS it. Every OTHER key is an ENTITY ATTRIBUTE name OR a top-level VALUE-OBJECT name (a business/developer name like `id` / `orderedOn` / `address`, NOT a physical column like `ordered_on`), and its value is the shared canonical `writeRowValue` — a scalar literal / explicit `null`, a one-key DB-COMPUTED marker (`{ computed: "maxPlusOne" }` / `{ increment: <n> }`), or the WHOLE embedded value-object document — REFERENCED from `write-instruction.schema.json` rather than redefined. The adapter classifies each field by its metamodel role and derives the emitted column list + ORDER from the target's Entity Layout view — never from JSON/YAML key order — so a marker-SHAPED value is a DB-computed marker vs a value-object document by MODEL ROLE, not by the value's SHAPE. A row object therefore CANNOT be `additionalProperties: false`: it names `observedVersion` and admits attribute / value-object keys via `additionalProperties`. The observed MILESTONE coordinates are the exception a row may never spell: a temporal write observes a whole predecessor milestone, which no flat row cell can name, so `observedTxStart` / `observedValidStart` ride beside the write (`when.observedTxStart` / `when.observedValidStart` — and, on a retry attempt, `observedTxStart` alone, since the edge form is single-attempt only) and a row authoring one is refused rather than stripped — stripping would silently discard the very coordinate the author meant to observe.

not.description: The observed milestone's own coordinate is never a row cell: it names the whole predecessor a temporal write observed, and it is authored beside the write.

observedVersion.description: The authentically observed optimistic-lock version (m-opt-lock). A reserved control key, NOT an attribute/column: everything taken from it is DERIVED, never authored — an UPDATE's advance (`observedVersion + 1`) and, under the effective Optimistic strategy, the `and version = ?` gate. Under the effective Locking strategy the current-transaction read that recorded it instead licenses the ungated write. Present on every versioned write against an EXISTING row — update or delete — since both strategies require authentic evidence; absent on a versioned insert and on a non-versioned write. This is FLUSH-TIME / materialization context — the durable instruction row (`write-instruction.schema.json#/$defs/writeRow`) forbids it, since the observation is never carried on the durable instruction (ADR 0013).

concurrencyStep.description: One node's step within a `when.concurrency` round. Carries its golden SQL as `statements` ({sql, binds} entries, dialect-keyed map form). On the concurrency-SUCCESS shape it additionally declares an explicit `kind`: a `read` step is fetched on its HELD session and its `expectRows` graded; a `write` step is executed and asserts only that it did not block/raise. `kind` is optional in this base def so the error/concurrency shape — whose only assertion is the classified error — carries no `kind`; the concurrency-success root branch requires it on every present step.

statements.description: This node step's golden SQL, as an ordered list of `{sql, binds}` statement entries (dialect-keyed map form).

kind.description: concurrency-success form only: the EXPLICIT read-vs-write discriminator the runners branch on (replacing the brittle SQL-verb sniffing). `read` — the step is fetched on its HELD session (`session.query`) and its rows graded against `expectRows`; `write` — the step is executed (`session.execute`) and asserts only that it did not block/raise. Structural: a `read` step MUST carry `expectRows`, a `write` step MUST omit it (the if/then below).

expectRows.description: concurrency-success form only: the rows this node's read MUST return on its HELD session. A read step (`kind: read`) MUST declare it; a write step (`kind: write`) omits it. Absent on the error/concurrency shape, whose only assertion is the classified error. A full-scalar shared read observes the object (INSTANCE-FORM / the object lane); every concurrency-success case reads the value-object-free `account`.

allOf.description: A read step (`kind: read`) MUST carry the rows it observes on its held session (`expectRows`), which the runner grades.
A write step (`kind: write`) MUST NOT carry `expectRows` — it asserts only that it did not block/raise, so there are no rows to grade.
